When no water could be found for the Asr ablution, the Prophet put his hand in a pot and water sprang from between his fingers until all had made ablution.
As-Sa'ib's aunt brought him ill to the Prophet, who prayed for him; he drank the leftover ablution water and saw the seal of prophethood between the Prophet's shoulders.
Water in a small painted pot brought to the Prophet sufficed for the ablution of eighty or more people.
Water sprang from between the Prophet's fingers in a shallow tumbler, enough for seventy to eighty people to make ablution.
The Prophet told his followers that their bowing and humility in prayer were not hidden from him, for he saw them from behind his back.
A woman's slave carpenter made the Prophet a pulpit, and when he sat on it the palm stem he used to preach beside cried until he embraced it.
With 130 companions, the Prophet bought a sheep from a pagan, gave everyone a piece of its roasted organs, and its meat filled two basins, with food left over.
Strong at ninety-four, As-Sa'ib bin Yazid credits his hearing and sight to the Prophet's prayer for him when sick, and he saw the seal between the Prophet's shoulders.
A woman's two waterskins served forty men, water flowed from the Prophet's fingers for hundreds, Hudaybiyyah's drained well refilled, small meals fed many, and Jabir's dates paid his father's debts.
When the Prophet moved to a new pulpit, the palm trunk he had preached beside cried like a child until he came and put his hand on it.
The Prophet foretold Adi a woman's safe journey from Al-Hira to the Ka'bah and Khosrau's treasures taken, which Adi saw, and urged shielding oneself from Hell with half a date.
When Khosrau perishes there will be no Khosrau after him, nor Caesar after Caesar, and their treasures will be spent in Allah's Cause.
The Prophet announced Ja'far's and Zaid's deaths before the news came and foretold Jabir's carpets; Umaiya, told the Prophet would kill him, went to Badr and was killed.
In the Prophet's lifetime the moon split in two when the Meccans asked for a miracle, and two companions walking on a dark night were lit by two lamp-like lights.
When the Meccans ask for a miracle, the moon splits in two with Hira between the halves, and at Mina the Prophet tells those with him to bear witness.
In the Prophet's lifetime the moon split into two parts when the people of Mecca asked for a sign, and he told them to witness it.
Abu Talha's few barley loaves, blessed by the Prophet, fed eighty men in tens, and one sheep fed all 130 men with some left over.
When a Jew refused Jabir more time on a date debt, the Prophet walked the garden and ate there, and the dates plucked repaid the debt with some left over.
Umm Sulaim's porridge from one mudd of barley fed forty men whom the Prophet called in by tens, and Anas looked to see if it had lessened.
At Asr, with only a little water in a vessel, water gushed from the Prophet's fingers and fourteen hundred men made ablution and drank from it.
Brought to the Prophet ill, the boy As-Sa'ib was blessed, drank the water of his ablution and saw the Seal of Prophethood between his shoulders.
When Abu Talha and Um Sulaim sent the hungry Prophet barley loaves, he came with his companions and blessed the bread, and seventy or eighty men ate their fill.
The Prophet was given concise speech of wide meaning, victory through awe and, in a dream, the world's treasure keys; unlike earlier prophets' miracles, his gift was revelation.
